newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks close firm, swept higher by property.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks close firm, swept higher by property.

text.p: A rebound in the property sector swept Hong Kong stocks to a firm close on Monday after heavy losses registered last week.
The Hang Seng Index closed on a gain of 102.00 points, or 0.80 percent, at 12,838.53. But turnover fell to HK$9.11 billion from HK$12.52 billion on Friday.
"I think the market has been oversold. It is just a technical rebound today," said Edward Chan, head of research at Amsteel Securities.
The Hang Seng fell 4.5 percent last week on fears about rising interest rates and the outlook for the property market.

U.S. February producer price data, released on Friday, helped calm some fears of an imminent rise in U.S. interest rates with a decline of 0.4 percent in the producer price index compared with expectations of a 0.1 percent fall.
Chan said the market had already discounted a 25 basis point hike in interest rates. "I don't think an interest rate hike, if any, will be high enough to dampen sentiment further," he said.

But analysts said investors were likely to remain cautious ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve's March 25 policy setting meeting. "The market will trade between 12,600 to 13,000 for the time being," said Vickers Ballas sales director Antony Mak.
"There has been no new money coming into the market since February so the market is not going anywhere," he said.

In the property sector Henderson Land Development Co Ltd, which is due to release interim results on Wednesday, rose HK$1.50 to HK$64.50, and Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd which releases interim results on Thursday, gained HK$0.75 to HK$84.25.

Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd rose HK$1.50 to HK$70.50. The company said it would offer an additional 125 units at its Laguna Verde residential development at HK$8,787 per square foot, up from an initial price of HK$8,286 per square foot.
It said about 2,000 potential buyers registered to buy an initial 78 units on offer.
Swire Pacific Ltd fell HK$0.75 to HK$60.75 on continued disappointment following its 1996 results.

Swire posted an 18.6 percent rise in 1996 net profit on Friday to HK$7.65 billion, including a HK$1.58 billion exceptional gain mostly from the sale of the JW Marriott Hotel Hong Kong and a stake in Hong Kong Dragon Airlines.
Hongkong Telecom rose HK$0.40 to HK$14.40. It said it would soft-launch its video-on-demand services in July.
Brokers said renewed talk that parent Cable and Wireless Plc would sell a Hongkong Telcom stake to a Chinese partner also boosted the stock.
